findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
Inspector observed the following facility items in need of repair:
1. The shelving in the walk-in cooler was observed rusted and in need of repair. Inspector recommends sealing the shelving with paint or replacing with coated shelving to prevent future rust accumulation.

2. The walk-in freezer has an accumulation of ice on food containers, walls, ceiling, floors, and shelving. Inspector recommends defrosting and cleaning the freezer. If accumulation persists, the freezer will require repair. 

Ensure these physical facility items are repaired prior to the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment:
Observed the following food items in the salad bar to be out of the appropriate temperature range : 
1. Sliced tomato (54F)
2. Cooked chicken (52F)
3. Sliced cucumber (51F)
4. Cut lettuce (41F)
5. Shredded cheese (high-moisture, 49F)
6. Ranch, 7 bottles (49-52F)
7. Italian dressing (52F)
8. French dressing (53F)
9. Fat-free ranch (52F)

All of these temperatures were measured with a probe thermometer. The cut tomato, shredded cheese, chicken, and salad dressings (original package labeled “refrigerate after opening”) were voluntarily discarded. The cut lettuce, since the temperature was at the safety threshold, was placed back into the walk-in cooler to ensure safe cold holding until lunch. Non-TCS foods were allowed to remain in the salad bar cooler.  The food had been in the salad bar cooler since 9am, and failed to reach a safe temperature. Lunch is served from 11am-1:30pm, so time as a control will be utilized for the new salad bar items. These items will be discarded again after lunch. PIC was informed that TCS foods can only be kept out of temp for a maximum of 4 hours and must be discarded after use. PIC was reminded that a time log must be maintained to record what time foods must be discarded after being placed on the salad bar.  PIC will be using time as a control until the salad bar cooler is repaired and can maintain foods at a temperature of 41F or below. For more information regarding the salad bar cooler, see violation #33.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.comment: Observed that the salad bar is failing to maintain food temperatures at 41F or below. The PIC is aware of the issue and will be submitting a work order to fix the salad bar. Until then, PIC will use time as a control for all time/temperature control for safety (TCS) foods on the salad bar. See violation #22 for more information regarding the impacted food in the salad bar cooler. A follow-up is scheduled for 10 days (3/6/2025) to check cold holding temperatures in the facility.

findings.title: Foods properly cooled
findings.citation_text:
750.140 - Lasagna from lunch was observed with surface and internal temperatures of 75F and 80F respectively. Lasagna was labeled with the date; time was not indicated on the label. Manager stated the product was pulled from the hot food line around 1p. Food was still above 70F after ~2.5hrs (time of temperature check was 322p). Lasagna was pulled from the cooler and discarded. Chicken breasts, also from lunch today, had an internal temperature of 49F. The plastic wrap for the pan used for chicken breasts was not tightly sealed. The plastic wrap over the pan of lasagna was tightly sealed, and a decent amount of condensation was observed. Proper cooling of cooked foods was discussed.

Cooked potentially hazardous foods shall be properly cooled from 135F to 70F w/in 2 hrs and from 70F to 41F/below w/in an additional 4 hrs. Total cooling time must not exceed 6hrs. Provide labels with both the date and time on cooling foods. Foods that are cooling should not be tightly covered until the product has finished cooling properly. Pans of cooling foods may be left with plastic wrap, foil, or lids slightly askew to allow for steam to vent off of cooling foods. Also, foods may be left uncovered while cooling in the walkin as long as the shelving above is clean and no raw foods are above the cooling product. When possible store cooling foods uncovered on the top shelf in the walkin. Utilize ice baths when necessary and stir foods frequently (batches of soup, etc.). Use a clean calibrated stem thermometer to monitor the temperature during the cooling process. Keep track of the time and temperature to ensure foods reach benchmark temperatures in the designated time frame for proper cooling.
**Educational handout on quick chill of cooked foods was provided**

The bucket was made by the worker with bleach earlier today, and it was possible another person remade the bucket at the quat dispenser prior to the dispenser malfunctioning. Employees need to be consistent with sanitizer used and stick to designated protocol (i.e. quat from the wall dispenser unless concentration is off then use bleach). Buckets were emptied, and manager stated bleach solutions would be remade prior to dinner shift this evening.

Maintain sanitizer at proper concentration. Always use test strips to verify concentration is correct (200ppm quat from wall dispenser & 100-200ppm chlorine for bleach solution). Change solutions every 2 to 4 hours or more often if solution and/or wiping cloths become heavily soiled.

750.1060 - A) Kitchen handsink temperature was fluctuating. Facility has hot water, but handsink is on a mixing valve. The handsink has hot and cold water handles underneath, but manager was unsure as to how each needed to be positioned to get a better balance to the water temperature. Maintenance will check the issue tomorrow.
(Also, clean the lower compartment behind the foot pedal).

B) Soda machine compressor was observed with condensation buildup, and puddling moisture was observed throughout the cabinet. The rug beneath the counter was also damp. Call for service was made to Pepsi. In the meantime, the cabinet was wiped out to minimize moisture buildup. Wipe out the cabinet as needed until repairs are made to eliminate the issue.

All plumbing shall be sized, installed, and maintained in accordance with applicable provisions of the Illinois State Plumbing Code.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.citation_text:
750.860 - A) Draw used for utensil storage at main prep table was soiled inside with splash and debris. Draw and all utensils were ran through the dish machine during the inspection.

B) Clean knives at food counter were stored with handles and food contact surfaces intermixed. Knives were ran through dish machine and placed in storage container all facing same direction with handles presented out.

Cleaned and sanitized utensils/equipment shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in a clean, dry location in a way that protects them from contamination by splash, dust and other means. Store utensils with handles presented out to avoid contact with food contact surfaces when retrieving for use.

Some repairs still need to be finalized around the dish machine**

B) Floor in front of new drink counter had sections missing tile. Maintenance workers are aware and plan to make repairs in the near future.

C) Small section of floor where electrical box was located for the old steam table/salad bar had holes and needed to be covered/sealed. Maintenance workers are aware and plan to make repairs in the near future.

Floors must be in good repair, constructed to facilitate easy cleaning, and maintained clean.

findings.citation_text:
750.120 - Tomatoes were rinsed and placed back in original cardboard box. Manager was advised the original box is not considered a clean surface for storage once tomatoes are rinsed.
Tomatoes were placed in a colander and rinsed again before finishing prep.

Foods shall be protected at all times. After cleaning fruit and vegetables make sure a clean, food grade container is used for storage.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.comment:
750.510, 512, & 160 - Employee went between tasks and did not change gloves. Food prep was discontinued, and employee went to dish area to fill sani-bucket. Employee returned to food prep without changing gloves. Upon request of inspector new gloves were put on by employee after hands were washed.

Gloves shall be single use and used for only 1 task.  Gloves shall be discarded when damaged, soiled or after an interruption in operations.
Hands must be properly washed before putting on gloves and between glove changes.

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.comment:
7550.830 - Sanitizer concentration at dish machine was 0ppm chlorine. Maintenance worker adjusted the chemical line (tube was not far enough down in the chemical bucket) and primed the machine. Sanitizer concentration was then observed to be at 100ppm after a full cycle of the dish machine.

All chemical sanitizers in a dish machine must meet the requirements of 21 CFR 178.1010 to ensure all items are properly sanitized. Chemicals musts dispense properly, and equipment/utensils must go through all cycles of ware washing process.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.citation_text:
750.810 - Sani-bucket in kitchen tested at 0ppm quat. Employee noted the bucket was changed within the last hour. Bucket was remade at proper concentration (200ppm).

Maintain quat solutions at 200ppm. The wall mounted dispenser should be calibrated to dispense the sanitizer at proper concentration. Make sure all employees and helpers know that water is not to be added to the solution from the faucet while filling the buckets.

Presence of insects/rodents.  Animals prohibited
findings.citation_text:
750.1160 - Approximately a dozen plus small flies (species unknown; possibly fruit flies) were observed at the time of inspection. Majority of flies were observed below the 2 part sink in the kitchen. A few flies were also observed on the wall between the prep table and the mixer in the kitchen, by the ice machine out front, and near the doorway to the dish room.  Management and staff were advised on areas to focus efforts on general cleaning and maintenance in order to minimize the presence of flies. If cleaning and maintenance alone do not alleviate the issue/help minimize the  number of flies then contact the pest control operator for service.
Eliminate potential food and water sources, and make repairs in areas that could serve as a hiding spot (i.e. loose damaged coving/damaged wall under 2 part sink).
Effective measures to minimize the presence of pests shall be utilized. Provide effective pest control.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.citation_text:
750.1200 & 1220 - A) Floor drain/cover below 2 part sink was soiled with buildup and old food debris. The debris could be serving as a potential food source for small flies observed in the area. Thoroughly clean the floor drain/cover (power wash/scrub).
B) Plastic baseboard was loose at floor to wall juncture below 2 part sink. A hole was observed near the base of the wall behind the coving. Make proper repairs to the wall and re-attach the coving under the 2 part sink.
C) Floor along the walls/in corners of kitchen (near 2 part sink, behind steamer, etc.) were soiled. Clean the floor in the kitchen, focusing effort along walls/in corners.
D) Floor and general surfaces between the hotbox and the cooler were soiled with debris and cobwebs. Clean the crevice between the aforementioned pieces of equipment.
Floors and drains/covers shall be kept clean and in good repair. The junctures between walls and floors shall be coved and sealed.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.comment:
750.140b - Jambalaya and rice observed cooling in the walkin cooler were dated, but the time was not marked on the containers. Temperatures were checked at ~2p. Surface temperatures were 97F and 80F, while internal temperatures were 135F and 120F respectively. Manager noted the products were pulled from the steam table after lunch around 1p. Benefit of doubt was given, and foods were kept. Products were separated into multiple pans, placed on ice baths, and stirred to rapidly drop the temperature throughout both foods. Proper cooling and labeling were discussed at length with Manager and staff. 
 Potentially hazardous food shall be labeled or tagged with date and time of preparation and rapidly cooled to an internal temperature of 41°F. (see general comments)

findings.title: Toxic items labeled and used properly
findings.citation_text:
750.1320 - Bleach solution in sanitizer bucket tested above 200ppm (test strip turned black). Solution was diluted to be at proper concentration of 100ppm. Maintain bleach solutions for wiping general surfaces at 100ppm (no higher than 200ppm), and maintain quat solutions at 200ppm. If sanitizer solutions are weak they aren't sanitizing surfaces, but if they are too strong then solutions are toxic. Make sure all staff know how to properly use test strips to verify sanitizing concentrations.
Poisonous materials shall not be used in any way that may pose a contamination hazard to food or clean equipment or pose a health hazard to staff and clients.

findings.title: Foods properly cooled
findings.citation_text: 750.140 - Meat sauce in 18 quart plastic pan (full to the top; heavy condensation inside the lid) made on 10/23 had surface temperature of 43F and internal temperature of 48F-50F. Meat sauce was discarded. A smaller portion of meat sauce in a stainless steel pan also with date mark of 10/23 had internal temperature of 40F-41F and was able to be kept for use. Kitchen Manager noted the meat sauce was cooled in an ice bath using a bain-marie prior to being placed in the pan in the walkin cooler. Cooling process was discussed with emphasis on separating products into shallow pans (especially thick foods and sauces), using ice baths, monitoring the temperatures to ensure foods are cooling properly, and leaving foods loosely covered until fully cooled. Cooked potentially hazardous foods shall be properly cooled from 135F to 70F within 2 hours and from 70F to 41F/below within an additional 4 hours. Total cooling time must not exceed 6hours.
